articles.title: Bihar 'alliance' redux in UP: Congress, SP play numbers game; can Priyanka do it for Rahul again?
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Can Akhilesh Yadav and Rahul Gandhi salvage a seat-sharing deal in time for the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections due early next year?
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Can Akhilesh Yadav and Rahul Gandhi salvage a seat-sharing deal in time for the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections due early next year? Or will the INDIA bloc end up doing a Bihar in UP?There seems to be an uncanny similarity between what happened in Bihar ahead of the 2025 assembly elections and what has been unfolding in UP for some time now. The Samajwadi Party and the Congress, the two INDIA bloc allies in UP, who together trumped the BJP in 2024 Lok Sabha elections, have been engaged in an open war of words over how many seats they want, or should get in an alliance for 2027. The numbers have been flying. There have been claims and counterclaims reviving memories of Bihar much to the delight of the BJP.Why a Bihar parallel?To understand that, let’s rewind to the 2025 Bihar assembly elections. The RJD and the Congress were upbeat about the prospects of INDIA bloc in the state. Rahul Gandhi’s vote-chori yatra, which saw great bonhomie between the two parties, had set the stage for the campaign and given the much-needed momentum to the INDIA bloc. But then came seat-sharing talks and the fight over numbers soon turned the bonhomie into an open war of words. The Congress wanted an increased share based on its improved Lok Sabha performance. Tejashwi was not willing to oblige. The two parties refused to budge from their positions. So much so, when Tejashwi went to file his nomination papers, no Congress leader was by his side. The two parties did eventually reach a consensus. But by then it was too late. Nitish Kumar and the BJP decimated the INDIA bloc in the elections. The RJD and the Congress registered their worst-ever performance in the state.Congress: Different state, new partner but same old storyOne would have hoped that Uttar Pradesh, one of the most important states for the opposition, would have been handled better or differently by both the parties, especially the Congress. Unfortunately that did not happen that way.The UP Congress leaders raised the demand for a respectable share of seats and also said that it wanted to be treated as an equal partner in any alliance. All familiar phrases we had heard in Bihar. However, they got an immediate pushback from the SP.When ending media speculation around numbers, Congress’s Uttar Pradesh in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam in October said that the party had sought 175-200 seats, the Samajwadi Party leaders were quick to openly remind the grand-old-party of its past performances in the state.Even as this back and forth played out, Akhilesh Yadav made it clear that “winnability” would be the only criterion for deciding seats. To drive home his message, he said this not once but several times.Akhilesh did not stop at that. In what appeared to be a measured dig at its ally, the SP chief during a TV programme, revealed the actual number of seats - 181 - that the Congress had sought. For a party that could win just 2 seats five years back in 2022 - the number 181 sounded not just unreasonable but also unrealistic. Interestingly, Akhilesh also announced that his party SP had already decided how many seats it will contest. Clearly, Akhilesh was not ready to cede any space till the actual talks started.Even when Akhilesh struck a conciliatory note, he did not budge from his winnability stand. "There is no talk of seat-sharing yet. INDIA alliance will fight together. Respecting each other, we will adjust the seats. The best of the candidates will contest," Akhilesh Yadav said.Meanwhile, to be fair to Congress, the party leadership did take several steps to signal that it was ready for a middle path. The party replaced its state unit president Ajay Rai, who was perceived as a hardliner vis-a-vis the SP, with Aradhna Misra (Mona), who enjoys a good rapport with Akhilesh. The party eventually also backed down its rhetoric and said “number of seats” was not important, the focus should be on “winning together.”Congress leadership finally intervenesThe Congress high command, which had all along been a passive observer in this seat numbers fight, finally woke up from its slumber and convened a meeting on November 16 with UP unit leaders.Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi and Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge discussed the party's preparations for the 2027 assembly elections with the state leaders."Today, I held an in-depth discussion with senior leaders of the Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee regarding the state's political situation and the upcoming assembly elections. The forthcoming elections in Uttar Pradesh will set a new direction for the nation's politics. The people of the state are looking toward change and wish to see social justice, equal opportunity, and the rights of marginalised sections strengthened. I am fully confident that the Congress party, in collaboration with the INDIA alliance, will present a strong alternative to the people of Uttar Pradesh," Congress president wrote on X after the meeting.Some reports claimed that Rahul Gandhi had told the leaders to focus on quality and not quantity, in a way endorsing what Akhilesh had said on winnability.There was a glimmer of hope after this meeting as some Congress leaders claimed that seat-sharing discussions would start from November 17. Reports that Akhilesh was to reach New Delhi on November 16 sparked speculations that seat-sharing talks will take off on November 17. But that did not happen. Responding to media queries at Delhi airport, Akhilesh said: “Seat sharing ko lekar ke kaheen koi baat nahi hai” (There is no talk of seat sharing yet).The book launch bonhomieThen came the launch ceremony of Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love. The function set the stage for perfect optics, with Akhilesh and his wife Dimple Yadav seated in the first row. News agencies citing sources reported that Rahul and Akhilesh had a word on the sidelines of the launch event. During this interaction, they discussed a potential alliance and seat-sharing for the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections.Sources indicated that a "draft" concerning seat-sharing was discussed during the conversation between the two leaders, though the specific details were not disclosed.Leaders from both parties are now expected to carry forward their discussions based on this draft and the formulas they have each proposed.UPCC working president Imran Masood later confirmed that his party’s top brass has had a word with the SP chief on the issue. “The SP chief has shared a ‘draft’ with our top leadership. We will make full preparations based on this draft,” Masood said.Priyanka to take centre stageThere are reports that Congress may pitchfork Priyanka Gandhi into the seat-sharing negotiations with the Samajwadi Party in UP. In the run up to the 2024 Lok Sabha elections when the seat sharing negotiations got stuck, reports suggested Priynaka used her personal rapport with Akhilesh to ensure a compromise was reached between the two parties.181 on wishlist, 24 on offerIrrespective of what is written on the draft, the road ahead will not be easy for the negotiators on both sides. A TOI report by Pervez Iqbal Siddiqui, chief of Bureau, TOI-Lucknow, suggests that the Samajwadi Party is likely to make an initial offer of around 24 seats to the Congress.The first round of negotiations between the two parties is expected to hover around 21 assembly seats where Congress candidates got 20,000-plus votes in the 2022 assembly polls, with an additional four seats where it was close to the 20,000-vote mark. Of these 21 seats, the SP will also retain seats with sitting SP MLAs and replace the count with seats where Congress had got between 10,000 and 20,000 votes.There will likely be very hard negotiations over assembly seats in Rae Bareli and Amethi. The two Lok sabha seats are with the Congress but in several assembly constituencies the SP had won elections in 2022. While the Congress will want all these seats in their stronghold, it is unlikely that the SP will leave them.Akhilesh reaches out to AAP, CPI(ML)Akhilesh Yadav is not just playing safe but also smart. Even as his party gears up for Congress talks, the SP chief has held separate meetings with AAP's Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh and CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharyya amid moves to explore seat-sharing for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly polls. Clearly, a message for the grand-old-party before the crucial talks happen.Incidentally, the AAP is outside the INDIA opposition bloc, with Singh announcing the party's exit from the alliance in July last year. The AAP and the CPI(ML) Liberation would wait for the SP to settle its seat-sharing arrangement with the Congress first before making their demands.Only silver lining(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(message,function(e){if(e.data[datawrapper-height]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(iframe);for(var n in e.data[datawrapper-height])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[datawrapper-height][n]+px;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();In the middle of all these manoeuvres, claims and counterclaims, there is one silver lining - leaders of both the parties have repeatedly asserted that the alliance will remain intact. Well, to be realistic neither the SP nor the Congress can afford to go it alone if they want to defeat the BJP. The Congress hopes to piggyback on SP’s strong presence to improve its performance. The SP, meanwhile, needs the Congress to woo the non-jatav Dalits and also sway the Muslims towards the INDIA bloc fold. But with the nitty-gritty of the alliance still under works, we are sure to see a lot of drama play out before the two allies eventually agree to a mutually acceptable seat-sharing deal.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Putin 'ready' to accept Nato-like shield for Ukraine, but with a catch
articles.summary: Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, citing Kyiv's ambition to join Nato as one of the major threats to its national security.
articles.body: Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, citing Kyiv's ambition to join Nato as one of the major threats to its national security.Nearly five years later, Moscow may be willing to accept Nato-like security guarantees for Ukraine, but only if Vladimir Putin gets to retain the territory captured by Russian forces.According to a report by the New York Post, citing an unnamed US official, Russia has signalled its willingness to consider security guarantees for Ukraine modelled on Nato's Article 4 and Article 5, without Kyiv becoming a formal member of the military alliance.The reported proposal would allow Ukraine to receive western security assurances against future Russian aggression while Moscow retains control over the Ukrainian territories occupied by its forces.The development comes amid renewed diplomatic efforts by US President Donald Trump to negotiate an end to the nearly five-year-long war, with American and Ukrainian officials holding discussions in Berlin.US special envoy Jared Kushner said Washington had made Russia comfortable with the idea of providing Ukraine with security guarantees based on Nato's Article 5 during discussions in Berlin.Kushner indicated that the proposed arrangement could offer Kyiv strong security assurances without requiring formal membership of the alliance. He also suggested that Moscow wanted to ensure another war did not break out after the current conflict.US special envoy Steve Witkoff described the possibility of Article 5-style guarantees as a "really, really big deal", indicating that Trump was open to such an arrangement. However, he acknowledged that significant work remained before a comprehensive agreement could be reached.Nato's Article 4 allows member countries to consult each other when their security is threatened, while Article 5 is its collective defence provision, treating an armed attack against one member as an attack against all and requiring allies to take action they consider necessary to assist it.Russia occupies nearly one-fifth of Ukraine's territoryRussia currently controls approximately 19 to 20 per cent of Ukraine's internationally recognised territory, including Crimea, which it annexed in 2014, and parts of several other Ukrainian regions.In the four regions it declared annexed in September 2022, Russian forces control nearly all of Luhansk, around 80 per cent of Donetsk, 76 per cent of Zaporizhzhia and approximately 70 per cent of Kherson, according to the Institute for the Study of War's November 11, 2026, assessment.Apart from these regions, Russian forces also hold smaller areas of Kharkiv, Sumy, Mykolaiv and Dnipropetrovsk. However, Moscow does not have complete military control over the four regions it claims to have annexed. Ukraine continues to hold parts of Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson.A ceasefire along the existing front lines could allow Russia to retain control over these occupied areas without requiring Ukraine to formally recognise them as Russian territory. This remains one of the biggest obstacles to a potential peace agreement.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In bizarre mix-up, Asaduddin Owaisi accorded guard of honour meant for Supreme Court judge in Uttar Pradesh
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: In a protocol mix-up, Saharanpur Police in Uttar Pradesh on Saturday mistakenly accorded a guard of honour to AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi
articles.body: NEW DELHI: In a protocol mix-up, Saharanpur Police in Uttar Pradesh on Saturday mistakenly accorded a guard of honour to AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi instead of a Supreme Court judge, who was the intended recipient of the ceremonial honour.According to reports, uniformed police personnel were stationed at the Saharanpur Circuit House to accord a guard of honour to the Supreme Court judge. However, before the judge arrived, the AIMIM chief reached the venue around 11.30 am with his convoy.Owaisi was in Saharanpur as part of a scheduled visit to meet Azad Samaj Party (Kanshiram) founder and Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad. The meeting was significant in the backdrop of the alliance between Owaisi's All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) and the Azad Samaj Party (Kanshiram) for the February-March 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections.Mistaking Owaisi's convoy and security detail for those of the scheduled dignitary, the deployed police personnel presented him with a guard of honour as the Hyderabad MP stepped out of his vehicle.Visuals showed Owaisi accepting the salute before entering the Circuit House. A video of the incident subsequently circulated widely on social media.Earlier in the day, Owaisi addressed a joint press conference with Azad in Saharanpur, where he claimed that their alliance, the Samajik Parivartan Morcha, had already caused "discomfort" and "distress" to Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath and Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav.Taking aim at the SP, Owaisi cited electoral outcomes from 2014, 2017, 2019, 2022 and 2024, questioning the party's record of contesting elections outside Uttar Pradesh."The reality is this: if you believe that the alliance you are talking about can defeat the BJP—well, it won't be able to. Look at 2014, 2017, 2019, 2022, and 2024—and then you accuse us of 'going there to contest.' The Samajwadi Party contested 640 seats across 13 states! You even contested in Andhra Pradesh. You won 114, and 111 of those were won from UP..." Owaisi said.He was referring to the SP's 114 MLAs across three states, including 111 in Uttar Pradesh, two in Maharashtra and one in Gujarat.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.body: NEW DELHI: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat on Saturday said that running an organisation for 100 years with discipline was a great spiritual endeavour. He underline the importance of dedication, service and commitment in sustaining an institution over generations.According to news agency ANI, Bhagwat was speaking at the birth centenary celebrations of Mata Bhagwati Devi Sharma at Shantikunj in Haridwar, Uttarakhand. The celebrations mark 100 years since the establishment of Akhand Deep.Addressing the gathering, Bhagwat said completing a century was not easy for any organisation, but carrying it forward with discipline was an even greater challenge. He said organisations often face neglect and difficulties during their journey, but continuous service and dedication eventually earn them society's trust, support and recognition.He also said there was no reason to doubt or worry about Sanatan Dharma, adding that the world was looking towards India for solutions to several contemporary challenges.According to Bhagwat, Indian culture and Sanatan thought have the potential to guide humanity. He described the work of the RSS and Gayatri Pariwar as being connected with a divine purpose, saying their continued expansion and success were a natural outcome of their efforts.Invoking Lord Hanuman as an example for volunteers, Bhagwat said selfless workers should dedicate themselves to the service of society and the preservation of Sanatan culture."Just as Lord Hanuman dedicated himself to the service of Lord Rama, every volunteer should similarly carry forward the work of Sanatan culture and social reconstruction with complete dedication," he said.The centenary celebrations mark 100 years since the establishment of Akhand Deep by Pandit Shriram Sharma Acharya, the founder of the Gayatri Pariwar movement. The sacred flame is associated with the organisation's spiritual mission and its emphasis on Gayatri Sadhana, self-discipline and social transformation.The celebrations also commemorate the 100th birth anniversary of Mata Bhagwati Devi Sharma, whose life was dedicated to spiritual practice, sacrifice and social reconstruction.The event began with the arrival of three sacred Kalash from Anwalkheda in Agra, Mathura and Haridwar, representing the birthplace, Tapobhoomi and Karmabhoomi of Pandit Shriram Sharma Acharya.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: He bought an abandoned California mining town for $1.4 million and moved in alone; eight years later, Brent Underwood is still restoring it while living without running water or phone service
articles.summary: Brent Underwood did not set out to spend years living in a remote mining settlement with no running water, mobile phone coverage or nearby grocery store.
articles.body: Brent Underwood did not set out to spend years living in a remote mining settlement with no running water, mobile phone coverage or nearby grocery store. Yet what began as an unusual property purchase in California has turned into a long-term commitment to bringing an abandoned town back to life. Since buying Cerro Gordo in 2018, Underwood has taken on the work of restoring its ageing buildings, maintaining the property and dealing with the difficulties of living thousands of feet above sea level. His life there is far removed from conventional city living. Winters can leave him cut off for days, supplies require careful planning and even ordinary household needs involve considerable effort.Brent Underwood's journey from Austin to California's remote mining townUnderwood's connection with Cerro Gordo began with an unexpected message from a friend in 2018. The friend had come across a property listing for the former silver-mining settlement, located in the mountains above Death Valley, and sent it to him largely as a joke.At the time, Underwood was looking for a new project. Originally from Tampa, Florida, he had already spent time living in New York City before moving to Austin, Texas, where he ran a bed-and-breakfast from a Victorian-era house.The mining town caught his attention almost immediately. After researching its background, he booked a flight to California to see the property for himself. Cerro Gordo appeared almost untouched by the passage of time, with old buildings scattered across the mountainous landscape. Its history and setting appealed to Underwood, who had grown up fascinated by the American West.
